newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates ease on strong offer.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates ease on strong offer.

text.p: Croatian money market rates eased amid strong offers of both term and call money on Wednesday and dealers said the trend was likely to continue.
"The most important news today is that the price of money is decreasing," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
She said call money was placed at 8.0 and 8.5 percent compared with yesterday's 9.5-9.9 percent range.
"Banks were offering money at even lower prices, but there was no demand," she said.
Morning trade by 0900 GMT totalled 13.8 million kuna leaving as much as a 100 million surplus in supply.
One- and two-month term rates were unchanged at 13 and 16 percent, with a single 14 percent two-week loan struck with a savings bank.
Banks repaid 60 million kuna of their Lombard borrowings from the central bank leaving a total of 26.1 million kuna. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
